subject: history

transcription: Agency-written introduction and background only: the five history paragraphs. The page H1 is supplied as the '# ' title line. Citation line, images and enlarge/download links, the DocsTeach block, the 'Teach with this document.' line, previous/next navigation and the full statutory transcript (AN ACT To enforce the fifteenth amendment..., ~33,000 chars) were removed (same treatment as the existing Milestone Documents pages). Bracketed case citations kept as printed. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: the Voting Rights Act of 1965 — signed August 6, 1965 (Congress passed it August 5), 95 years after the 15th Amendment; the obstacles (poll taxes, literacy tests, harassment and violence) and the 1964 demonstrations, the Mississippi murders and Selma; what the act did (outlawed literacy tests, federal examiners, Section 5 preclearance for covered jurisdictions, Section 2 nationwide prohibition mirroring the 15th Amendment); the 24th Amendment (1964) poll-tax ban and Harper v. Virginia State Board of Elections, 383 U.S. 663 (1966); immediate impact numbers (a quarter of a million new Black voters registered by the end of 1965, one-third by federal examiners; by the end of 1966 only four of 13 southern states below 50 percent registration); readoption in 1970, 1975 and 1982; and the 2013 decision striking the oversight formula. Fits timeline ordering, quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the numbers and dates, and a compare table of the act's sections.
